request: Before any capital buffers or other add-ons, what minimum common equity tier 1, tier 1, total capital and leverage ratios must a Board-regulated institution maintain under the text of 12 CFR Part 217 reproduced on the cited page?
On days when direct-transmission filings are accepted, what is the daily submission window in the text of 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) reproduced on the cited page, and which days are excluded?

In the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 adopted on 15 May 2014, by when must an investment firm report complete and accurate details of transactions it has executed to the competent authority?
For 2025, according to IRS Publication 550, what is the Net Investment Income Tax rate, and to which amount is that rate applied?
In the original text of Directive 2009/138/EC, what probability and time horizon are used to describe the Solvency Capital Requirement, and what equivalent ruin frequency is stated?

An FDIC-supervised institution holds $80 million fair value of level 2A liquid assets and $30 million fair value of level 2B liquid assets as of the calculation date, and all are eligible HQLA. Ignoring other caps and adjustments, what level 2A and level 2B liquid asset amounts result under the text of 12 CFR Part 329 reproduced on the cited page, and what is their sum?

A covered company subject to the single-counterparty credit limits in 12 CFR Part 252 has $40 billion of tier 1 capital and an $11 billion aggregate net credit exposure to one counterparty. As in force on 2026-11-21, what is its 25% exposure cap in dollars, by how much does the exposure exceed that cap, and is the separate 5% economic-interdependence and control-relationship assessment triggered?

A registrant's named executive officer has perquisites and personal benefits totalling $120,000, including items worth $24,000 and $26,000. Under 17 CFR 229.402(c) as in force on 2026-11-21, may the registrant exclude perquisites altogether, what is the footnote quantification threshold, and which of those two items must be quantified?

An advanced approaches national bank that is not a savings and loan holding company has a legacy checklist using the OCC transition standards for calendar year 2014. What minimum common equity tier 1 and tier 1 capital ratios applied from January 1 through December 31, 2014, and what are the corresponding minimum ratios in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page? Ignore buffers and other add-ons.

According to HMRC's rates and allowances guidance, for non-ring fence profits under the rules from 1 April 2023, is there still a single Corporation Tax rate? State the rate for profits of £50,000 or less, the main rate for profits above £250,000, and the treatment of profits between those amounts.
A Federal branch of a foreign bank asks which minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio 12 CFR Part 3 imposes directly on that branch. What is the answer as in force on 2026-11-21?

An institution is scoping the annual privacy notice obligation in 17 CFR Part 248, subpart A. Apart from § 248.30(b), does that subpart cover information about companies or information about individuals who obtain financial products or services primarily for business purposes, as in force on 2026-11-21?

An EU payment institution provides only the payment service listed in point (6) of Annex I to the EU payment-services directive adopted in 2015. Under that directive's original text, what minimum capital must it maintain at all times?

Under the original text of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012, by when must details of a derivative contract's conclusion, modification or termination be reported, and how long must counterparties keep records of a contract and its modifications?

quotes.whole:
§§ 217.4-217.9
[Reserved]
Subpart B—Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers
§ 217.10
Minimum capital requirements.
(a)
Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
(iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
(v) For advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.
(2) A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in § 217.12), that is subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework (as defined § 217.12), is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in this paragraph (a) of this section.
(b)
Standardized capital ratio calculations.
Other than as provided in paragraph (c) of this section:
(1)
Common equity tier 1 capital ratio.
A Board-regulated institution's common equity tier 1 capital ratio is the ratio of the Board-regulated institution's common equity tier 1 capital to standardized total risk-weighted assets;
(2)
Tier 1 capital ratio.

§§ 217.4-217.9 [Reserved]
Subpart B—Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers
§ 217.10 Minimum capital requirements.
(a) Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.

verdict.summary:
# Regulatory Capital Minimums Memo — 12 CFR Part 217 (Subpart B, § 217.10)

**Status:** Draft for qualified finance or accounting professional review. This memo is not financial, tax, or investment advice.

**Grounding & Basis Note:** The request refers to "the cited page" without specifying a URL or publication date in the prompt text. This analysis verifies all figures against the official text of 12 CFR Part 217 reproduced in the current eCFR (`ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-217`, `section-217.10`, and `section-217.11`, fetched 2026-11-22) and the 2025 and 2026 Code of Federal Regulations annual editions (`CFR-2025-title12-vol2-part217.xml` and `CFR-2026-title12-vol2-part217.xml`, fetched 2026-11-22). All four sources contain identical text for § 217.10(a)(1). All figures below are dimensionless regulatory ratio percentages (not currency amounts), stated on a regulatory capital basis for the current post-transition period (see historical transition note below).

---

## 1. Minimum Capital Ratios (Before Buffers or Other Add-Ons)

Under **12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)**, before applying any capital conservation buffer, stress capital buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, GSIB surcharge, or leverage buffer under § 217.11, a Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:

| Capital Ratio | Minimum Requirement | Unit / Currency | Basis | Exact Regulatory Citation |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| **Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio** | **4.5** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(i) |
| **Tier 1 capital ratio** | **6** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(ii) |
| **Total capital ratio** | **8** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory capital / risk-weighted assets (standardized, or lower of standardized and advanced approaches) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(iii) |
| **Leverage ratio** | **4** | Percent (ratio; N/A currency) | Regulatory Tier 1 leverage measure (non-risk-weighted) | 12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(iv) |

### Additional Conditional Minimum in § 217.10(a)(1)
- **Supplementary Leverage Ratio (SLR) — 3 percent** (`12 CFR § 217.10(a)(1)(v)`): Applicable **only** to "advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions." While not one of the four general ratios named in the request, it appears in the same § 217.10(a)(1) list of base minimum capital ratios.

---

## 2. Ratio Calculation Bases & Institutional Applicability in § 217.10

- **Standardized Capital Ratio Calculations (`12 CFR § 217.10(b)`):**
  - *CET1 capital ratio (`§ 217.10(b)(1)`):* CET1 capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**.
  - *Tier 1 capital ratio (`§ 217.10(b)(2)`):* Tier 1 capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**.
  - *(Note: Standardized total capital and leverage ratio mechanics are cross-referenced via `§ 217.11(a)` to `§ 217.10(b)(3)` and `(c)`.)*
- **Advanced Approaches Capital Ratio Calculations (`12 CFR § 217.10(d)`):**
  - Once an advanced approaches Board-regulated institution completes the parallel run process and receives Board notification under `§ 217.121(d)`, its CET1 (`§ 217.10(d)(1)`), Tier 1 (`§ 217.10(d)(2)`), and Total Capital (`§ 217.10(d)(3)`) ratios are each the **lower of**:
    1. The respective capital divided by **standardized total risk-weighted assets**; and
    2. The respective capital divided by **advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets**.
- **Community Bank Leverage Ratio (CBLR) Framework (`12 CFR § 217.10(a)(2)`):**
  - A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in `§ 217.12`) that is subject to the CBLR framework is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in `§ 217.10(a)`.
- **Insurance Depository Institution Holding Companies (`12 CFR § 217.10(f)(1)`):**
  - An insurance bank holding company or insurance savings and loan holding company that is a state-regulated insurer and subject to subpart J of Part 217 is not required to meet the risk-based minimum capital ratio requirements in `§ 217.10(a)(1)(i)–(iii)`.
- **General Capital Adequacy Requirement (`12 CFR § 217.10(e)`):**
  - Notwithstanding the numerical minimums, a Board-regulated institution must maintain capital commensurate with the level and nature of all risks to which it is exposed (`§ 217.10(e)(1)`) and maintain an internal capital adequacy assessment process and strategy (`§ 217.10(e)(2)`).

---

## 3. Buffers and Add-Ons Excluded per Constraint (12 CFR § 217.11)

To confirm the boundary between the base minimums and "capital buffers or other add-ons," `12 CFR § 217.11` layers payout-limiting buffers on top of the `§ 217.10(a)` minimums (specifically computing buffers as actual capital ratios *minus* the `§ 217.10(a)` minimum requirements). Per the request constraint, the following § 217.11 add-ons are **excluded** from the 4.5% / 6% / 8% / 4% minimums above:
- **Capital Conservation Buffer / Stress Capital Buffer Requirement (`§ 217.11(a)`):** For institutions subject to `12 CFR 225.8` or `238.170`, composed solely of CET1 capital (with a 2.5% default stress capital buffer requirement if not yet assigned).
- **Countercyclical Capital Buffer (`§ 217.11(b)(2)(iii)`):** Adjustable by the Board between 0% and 2.5% of risk-weighted assets for U.S. credit exposures.
- **GSIB Surcharge (`§ 217.11(d)`):** Calculated under subpart H for global systemically important BHCs.
- **Leverage Buffer (`§ 217.11(c)(4)`, `§ 217.11(f)`):** Composed solely of Tier 1 capital, measured as the supplementary leverage ratio minus 3% for GSIB BHCs and their state member bank subsidiaries (with the state member bank leverage buffer requirement equal to the lesser of 1.0% or 50% of the parent GSIB's method 1 surcharge under `§ 217.403(b)`).

---

## 4. Reviewer Verification Check: Historical Transition Provision (§ 217.300)

Because the prompt did not include the exact link to "the cited page," the reviewer should confirm that the cited page reproduces the current/post-2015 Part 217 rule (`§ 217.10(a)(1)`). Under the historical transition provisions in **`12 CFR § 217.300`**, for the **January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014** transition period only, the minimum ratios were **4 percent CET1**, **5.5 percent Tier 1**, **8 percent total capital**, and **4 percent leverage**. All current and 2025–2026 CFR editions of `§ 217.10(a)(1)` state **4.5 percent CET1**, **6 percent Tier 1**, **8 percent total capital**, and **4 percent leverage**.

Editorial Note on Part 240




Editorial Note:


Nomenclature changes to part 240 appear at 57 FR 36501, Aug. 13, 1992, and 57 FR 47409, Oct. 16, 1992.






§ 240.0-2 Business hours of the Commission.




(a) The principal office of the Commission, at 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549, is open each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever currently is in effect in Washington, DC, provided that hours for the filing of documents pursuant to the Act or the rules and regulations thereunder are as set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.






(b) Submissions made in paper.  Paper documents filed with or otherwise furnished to the Commission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.






(c) Electronic filings.  Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.

        § 240.0-2
        Business hours of the Commission.
        
            (a) The principal office of the Commission, at 100 F Street, NE, Washington, DC 20549, is open each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever currently is in effect in Washington, DC,

             hours for the filing of documents pursuant to the Act or the rules and regulations thereunder are as set forth in paragraphs (b) and (c) of this section.

            (b) 
            Submissions made in paper.
             Paper documents filed with or otherwise furnished to the Commission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays, from 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.
        
        
            (c) 
            Electronic filings.
             Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.

REGULATORY SUBMISSION SCHEDULE MEMORANDUM (DRAFT FOR QUALIFIED PROFESSIONAL REVIEW)
Notice: This output is a draft for a qualified finance, accounting, or compliance professional to review. It is not financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

1. Scope, Source, and Basis
- Regulation Cited: 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) ("Business hours of the Commission — Electronic filings").
- Source Texts Reviewed:
  * Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR), current through fetch timestamp 2026-11-22T23:28:53Z (https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/part-240/section-240.0-2; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-240/subpart-A/subject-group-ECFRf2ef38fa463cdfa/section-240.0-2).
  * GovInfo Code of Federal Regulations, Title 17, Volume 4, Edition Date 2025-04-01 (https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol4/xhtml/CFR-2025-title17-vol4-sec240-0-2.html).
  * Amendment history noted on source pages: [58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023].
- Basis & Currency: All figures represent clock times (no monetary currency applies) on the regulatory basis of Eastern Standard Time (EST) or Eastern Daylight Saving Time (EDT), whichever is currently in effect in Washington, DC, for the current eCFR / 2025-04-01 CFR period.

2. Verbatim Text of 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c)
"(c) Electronic filings. Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect."

3. Findings and Schedule
- Ask 2 — Daily Submission Window (on accepted days):
  * Window: 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect.
  * Arithmetic Check (Daily Duration): 10:00 p.m. (22:00) minus 6:00 a.m. (06:00) = 16 hours (960 minutes) per accepted day. Source: 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c).
- Ask 4 — Excluded Days:
  * Excluded Days: Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays. Source: 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c).
  * Weekly Day-Count Reconciliation (Standard Non-Holiday Week): 7 calendar days total minus 2 excluded weekend days (Saturday, Sunday) = 5 accepted submission days (Monday through Friday), further reduced by 1 day for each Federal holiday falling on a weekday.

4. Related Context Noted in the Cited Rule Text
- Comparison to Principal Office and Paper Hours (17 CFR § 240.0-2(a)–(b)): Principal office hours are 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. (8.5 hours), and paper submission hours are 8:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. (9.5 hours), both subject to the same exclusions (Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays) and EST/EDT basis. Direct-transmission electronic filings therefore receive an additional 6.5 hours daily relative to paper submissions (16.0 hours - 9.5 hours = 6.5 hours; 2 hours earlier opening from 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 a.m., plus 4.5 hours later closing from 5:30 p.m. to 10:00 p.m.).
- Section 240.0-2(c) states only the general submission acceptance window and excluded days; specific filing-date cutoff rules for particular forms (such as Form 19b-4 under 17 CFR § 240.19b-4, which applies a 5:30 p.m. EST/EDT cutoff for same-business-day filing status) are governed by their respective rule sections.

Article 26Obligation to report transactions
1.Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments shall report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent authority as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the following working day.
The competent authorities shall, in accordance with Article 85 of Directive 2014/65/EU, establish the necessary arrangements in order to ensure that the competent authority of the most relevant market in terms of liquidity for those financial instruments also receives that information.
The competent authorities shall make available to ESMA, upon request, any information reported in accordance with this Article.

verdict.summary:
COMPLIANCE REVIEW MEMORANDUM (DRAFT)

Notice: This output is a draft prepared for review by a qualified finance, accounting, or compliance professional. It does not constitute financial, tax, investment, or legal advice.

1. Regulatory Determination (Ask 1 & Ask 2)
- Instrument: Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council (original text adopted at Brussels on 15 May 2014).
- Provision: Title IV, Article 26(1) (Obligation to report transactions).
- Reporting Deadline: An investment firm which executes transactions in financial instruments must report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent authority "as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the following working day."

2. Verbatim Statutory Text
Article 26(1), first subparagraph (as originally adopted on 15 May 2014):
"1. Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments shall report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent authority as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the following working day."

3. Period, Currency, Basis, and Arithmetic
- Period: From transaction execution (Day 0 / T) through the close of the following working day (T + 1 working day).
- Currency: Not applicable (statutory timing requirement rather than a monetary figure).
- Basis: Original EU adopted legal text as at 15 May 2014 (excluding subsequent amendments and Level 2 delegated/implementing measures).
- Arithmetic / Timing Calculation: Execution Day (T) + 1 working day (measured to the close of that following working day) = maximum outer deadline; subject to the primary requirement to report "as quickly as possible" inside that window.

4. Supporting Compliance Context from the Original 15 May 2014 Text
- Responsibility and Submission Channels (Article 26(7)): Reports may be submitted by the investment firm itself, an Approved Reporting Mechanism (ARM) acting on its behalf, the trading venue through whose system the transaction was completed, or a trade repository registered under Article 9 of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 approved as an ARM (provided transmission to the competent authority occurs within the Article 26(1) time limit). Regardless of channel, investment firms retain responsibility for the completeness, accuracy, and timely submission of the reports.
- Error Correction (Article 26(7)): Where errors or omissions occur, the ARM, investment firm, or trading venue reporting the transaction must correct the information and submit a corrected report to the competent authority.
- Level 2 Mandate (Article 26(9)): ESMA was mandated to develop and submit draft regulatory technical standards to the Commission by 3 July 2015 to specify technical reporting details.
- Original Application Date (Final Provisions): The original 15 May 2014 adopted text states, "This Regulation shall apply from 3 January 2017." (Note: subsequent EU legislation amended the application date and certain provisions; a separate review of the consolidated current text is required for live operational compliance.)

5. Sources
- Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, Article 26 (Original as adopted): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26/adopted
- Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, Body (Point in time view as at 15/05/2014): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/body/2014-05-15
- Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, Title IV (Original as adopted): https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/title/IV/adopted

Capital Gain Tax Rates
The tax rates that apply to a net capital gain are generally lower than the tax rates that apply to other income. These lower rates are called the maximum capital gain rates.
The term “net capital gain” means the amount by which your net long-term capital gain for the year is more than your net short-term capital loss.
For 2025, the maximum capital gain rates are 0%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and 28%. See Table 4-4 for details.
Tip:
If you figure your tax using the maximum capital gain rate and the regular tax computation results in a lower tax, the regular tax computation applies.

Tax on unearned income of certain children.
Form 8615 must be filed for any child who meets all of the following conditions.
The child has more than $2,700 of unearned income.
The child is required to file a tax return.
The child either:
Was under age 18 at the end of 2025,
Was age 18 at the end of 2025 and didn’t have earned income that was more than half of the child's support, or
Was a full-time student at least age 19 and under age 24 at the end of 2025 and didn’t have earned income that was more than half of the child's support.
At least one of the child's parents was alive at the end of 2025.
The child doesn’t file a joint return for 2025.
See Form 8615 and its instructions for details.

quotes.text:
Capital Gain Tax Rates
The tax rates that apply to a net capital gain are generally lower than the tax rates that apply to other income. These lower rates are called the maximum capital gain rates.
The term “net capital gain” means the amount by which your net long-term capital gain for the year is more than your net short-term capital loss.
For 2025, the maximum capital gain rates are 0%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and 28%. See Table 4-4 for details.
Tip:
If you figure your tax using the maximum capital gain rate and the regular tax computation results in a lower tax, the regular tax computation applies.
quotes.whole:
Capital Gain Tax Rates
The tax rates that apply to a net capital gain are generally lower than the tax rates that apply to other income. These lower rates are called the maximum capital gain rates.
The term “net capital gain” means the amount by which your net long-term capital gain for the year is more than your net short-term capital loss.
For 2025, the maximum capital gain rates are 0%, 15%, 20%, 25%, and 28%. See Table 4-4 for details.
Tip:
If you figure your tax using the maximum capital gain rate and the regular tax computation results in a lower tax, the regular tax computation applies.
Example.
All of your net capital gain is from selling collectibles, so the capital gain rate would be 28%. If you are otherwise subject to a rate lower than 28%, the 28% rate does not apply.

quotes.whole:
When you figure the amount of any capital loss carry-over to the next year, you must take the current year's al-lowable deduction into account, whether or not you
claimed it and whether or not you filed a return for the cur-rent year.
When you carry over a loss, it remains long-term or
short-term. A long-term capital loss you carry over to the
next tax year will reduce that year's long-term capital gains
before it reduces that year's short-term capital gains.
Figuring your carryover. The amount of your capital
loss carryover is the amount of your total net loss that is
more than the lesser of:
1. Your allowable capital loss deduction for the year, or
2. Your taxable income increased by your allowable cap-ital loss deduction for the year.
If your deductions are more than your gross income for
the tax year, use your negative taxable income in figuring
the amount in (2) above.

A 3.8 percent net investment income tax (NIIT) applies to individuals, estates, and trusts that have net investment income above applicable threshold amounts.
Individuals
In the case of an individual, the NIIT is 3.8 percent on the lesser of:
the net investment income, or
the excess of modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) over the following threshold amounts:
$250,000 for married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse
$125,000 for married filing separately
$200,000 for single or head of household
Estates and trusts
In the case of an estate or trust, the NIIT is 3.8 percent on the lesser of:
the undistributed net investment income, or
the excess (if any) of:
the adjusted gross income over the dollar amount at which the highest tax bracket begins for an estate or trust for the tax year. (For estates and trusts, the 2025 threshold is $15,650. If the estate or trust’s AGI is below $15,650, it is not subject to the NIIT.)

quotes.whole:
Reporting NIIT
Compute the tax on Form 8960, Net Investment Income Tax—Individuals, Estates, and Trusts.
Individuals report this tax on Form 1040, U.S. Individual Income Tax Return or Form 1040-SR, U.S. Tax Return for Seniors;
Estates and trusts report this tax on Form 1041, U.S. Income Tax Return for Estates and Trusts.
Tax withholding and estimated tax
Taxpayers may need to increase their income tax withholding or estimated taxes because of any additional tax liability from the NIIT to avoid certain penalties. The Tax Withholding Estimator can be used to help determine necessary changes in withholding by your employer or see our Estimated taxes page for resources to help you recalculate those payments. See Publication 505, Tax Withholding and Estimated Tax for more information in either instance.
Additional information
For additional information, refer to the Instructions for Form 8960 PDF and to Questions and answers on the net investment income tax.

DRAFT FOR PROFESSIONAL REVIEW — NOT FINANCIAL, TAX, OR INVESTMENT ADVICE

TECHNICAL ACCOUNTING & TAX REFERENCE SCHEDULE: NET INVESTMENT INCOME TAX (NIIT)
Period: Tax Year 2025 (Calendar-Year Basis, for use in preparing 2025 U.S. federal income tax returns)
Currency: U.S. Dollars (USD) for monetary thresholds; statutory percentage (%) for tax rate
Primary Grounding: IRS Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses (Including Capital Gains and Losses) — "For use in preparing 2025 Returns" (IRS.gov/publications/p550; PDF cycle01 dated 03/06/2026; IRS list revision date 03/09/2026), Chapter 1, "General Information — Net investment income tax (NIIT)"

1. Executive Summary (Direct Answers to Asks)
- Ask 1 [Constraint — Authority]: All primary rate, base, and individual threshold figures below are sourced directly from IRS Publication 550 (2025).
- Ask 2 [NIIT Rate]: 3.8% (statutory flat percentage; Tax Year 2025; Source: IRS Publication 550 (2025), "Net investment income tax (NIIT)").
- Ask 3 [Tax Base / Amount to Which the Rate Is Applied]: The lesser of:
  (a) the taxpayer's net investment income (NII), or
  (b) the amount of the taxpayer's modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that exceeds the applicable threshold amount based on filing status.
  (Source: IRS Publication 550 (2025), "Net investment income tax (NIIT)").

2. Authoritative Rate, Base Formula, and Arithmetic
- Statutory Rate: 3.8% (0.038)
  - Period / Basis: Tax Year 2025, U.S. federal statutory rate (IRC section 1411, as cited in IRS Pub. 550 (2025)).
- Base Arithmetic (Individual Taxpayers):
  - Excess MAGI (USD) = max($0, MAGI - Applicable Filing-Status Threshold)
  - NIIT Taxable Base (USD) = min(Net Investment Income, Excess MAGI)
  - NIIT Liability (USD) = 3.8% x NIIT Taxable Base
  (If MAGI is at or below the applicable threshold, Excess MAGI = $0, NIIT Taxable Base = $0, and NIIT Liability = $0.)

3. Applicable MAGI Threshold Schedule (Tax Year 2025, USD)
Per IRS Publication 550 (2025), "Net investment income tax (NIIT)" table (Basis: 2025 statutory individual filing-status thresholds, unindexed for inflation):
- Married Filing Jointly or Qualifying Surviving Spouse: $250,000 USD (Source: IRS Pub. 550 (2025))
- Married Filing Separately: $125,000 USD (Source: IRS Pub. 550 (2025))
- Single or Head of Household: $200,000 USD (Source: IRS Pub. 550 (2025))

4. Scope & Primary Authority Cross-References
- Publication 550 (2025) directs taxpayers to Internal Revenue Code (IRC) section 1411, Form 8960 (Net Investment Income Tax—Individuals, Estates, and Trusts), and the Instructions for Form 8960 for complete computational rules and definitions.
- Note on Estates and Trusts (Supplementary IRS Source): Publication 550 (2025) lists only the individual filing-status thresholds above. For completeness under Form 8960 / IRS Tax Topic No. 559 (reviewed 09/24/2026), for estates and trusts in Tax Year 2025, the same 3.8% rate applies to the lesser of undistributed net investment income or the excess of adjusted gross income over $15,650 USD (the 2025 dollar amount where the highest estate/trust tax bracket begins).
- Note on "Net Investment Income" Definition: For NIIT calculation, compute NII on Form 8960 per its instructions (Publication 550 also defines general "net investment income" in Chapter 3 for the investment interest expense deduction limit—investment income minus allowed investment expenses other than interest expense—but Form 8960 governs the exact IRC section 1411 NIIT base).

The tax rates that apply to a net capital gain are generally lower than the tax rates that apply to other income. These lower rates are called the maximum capital gain rates.

### Regulatory Reference Memo: Solvency Capital Requirement (SCR) Calibration in Directive 2009/138/EC (Original Adopted Text)

*Notice: This output is a reference draft prepared for review by a qualified finance, actuarial, or regulatory professional. It does not constitute legal, regulatory, financial, tax, or investment advice.*

---

#### 1. Summary of Required Figures

| Ask | Parameter | Value in Original Text | Unit / Basis / Period / Currency | Authoritative Source in Original Text |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **2** | **Probability (Confidence Level)** | **99.5%** (printed as `99,5 %`) | Unit: `%` (probability / VaR confidence level). Basis: Regulatory VaR of basic own funds / probability of meeting obligations. Period: One-year risk horizon. Currency: N/A (dimensionless). | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Article 101(3)** & **Recital (64)** |
| **2** | **Time Horizon** | **One-year period** (with new business expected over the **following 12 months**) | Unit: `year` (`1 year` / `12 months`). Basis: Going-concern calibration horizon for unexpected losses on existing business and expected new business. Currency: N/A. | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Article 101(3)** |
| **3** | **Equivalent Ruin Frequency** | **Once in every 200 cases** (1-in-200) | Unit: `cases` (stated verbatim as `once in every 200 cases`; corresponds to a 200-year return period given the one-year horizon in Art. 101(3)). Basis: Economic capital threshold. Currency: N/A. | Directive 2009/138/EC (as adopted 25 Nov 2009), **Recital (64)** |

---

#### 2. Verbatim Citations from the Original Adopted Text (25 November 2009)

Source: *Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast)*, Original English Official Journal / As-adopted PDF (`eudr_20090138_adopted_en.pdf`).

1. **Article 101(3) — Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement** (Title I, Chapter VI, Section 4, Subsection 1):
   > "The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.
   > 
   > It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period."

2. **Recital (64) — Equivalent Probability and Ruin Frequency**:
   > "(64) In order to promote good risk management and align regulatory capital requirements with industry practices, the Solvency Capital Requirement should be determined as the economic capital to be held by insurance and reinsurance undertakings in order to ensure that ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases or, alternatively, that those undertakings will still be in a position, with a probability of at least 99,5 %, to meet their obligations to policy [holders and beneficiaries...]"

*(Note for completeness: Under **Article 122(1)**, undertakings using an internal model may use a different time period or risk measure than Article 101(3) provided the resulting outputs yield an equivalent level of protection for policyholders and beneficiaries.)*

---

#### 3. Arithmetic Reconciliation of Confidence Level and Ruin Frequency

- **Stated confidence level ($p$):** $99.5\% = 0.995$ (Source: Article 101(3); Recital (64)).
- **Implied one-year ruin / exceedance probability ($1 - p$):**
  $$1 - 0.995 = 0.005 = 0.5\%$$
- **Equivalent ruin frequency (return period):**
  $$\frac{1}{1 - 0.995} = \frac{1}{0.005} = 200$$
- **Reconciliation to Recital (64):** A $0.5\%$ probability of exceedance equals $1$ event per $200$ cases, matching the Directive's exact wording in Recital (64) ("ruin occurs no more often than once in every 200 cases"). Combined with the "one-year period" specified in Article 101(3), this represents an expected ruin frequency of no more than once every 200 years.

quotes.whole: An asset is a level 2A liquid asset if the asset is liquid and readily-marketable and is one of the following types of assets: (1) A security issued by, or guaranteed as to the timely payment of principal and interest by, a U.S. government-sponsored enterprise, that is investment grade under 12 CFR part 1 as of the calculation date, provided that the claim is senior to preferred stock; or (2) A security that is issued by, or guaranteed as to the timely payment of principal and interest by, a sovereign entity or multilateral development bank that is: (i) Not included in level 1 liquid assets; (ii) Assigned no higher than a 20 percent risk weight under subpart D of 12 CFR part 324 as of the calculation date; (iii) Issued or guaranteed by an entity whose obligations have a proven record as a reliable source of liquidity in repurchase or sales markets during stressed market conditions, as demonstrated by: (A) The market price of the security or equivalent securities of the issuer declining by no more than 10 percent during a 30 calendar-day period of significant stress, or (B) The market haircut demanded by counterparties to secured lending and secured funding transactions that are collateralized by the security or equivalent securities of the issuer increasing by no more than 10 percentage points during a 30 calendar-day period of significant stress; and (iv) Not an obligation of a financial sector entity, and not an obligation of a consolidated subsidiary of a financial sector entity.

DRAFT FOR QUALIFIED FINANCE OR ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL REVIEW ONLY. THIS IS NOT FINANCIAL, TAX, OR INVESTMENT ADVICE.

================================================================================
MEMORANDUM & CALCULATION SCHEDULE: HQLA LEVEL 2A AND LEVEL 2B LIQUID ASSET AMOUNTS
================================================================================
Entity Type: FDIC-Supervised Institution (per 12 CFR § 329.3)
Regulatory Authority: 12 CFR Part 329 (Liquidity Risk Measurement Standards), Subpart C, § 329.21
Period / Valuation Point: As of the Calculation Date (single-date Liquidity Coverage Ratio calculation point under 12 CFR § 329.3 and § 329.21(a)-(b))
Currency: U.S. Dollars (USD), reported in USD millions
Measurement Basis: Fair value as determined under U.S. GAAP (per 12 CFR § 329.3), unadjusted and pre-cap (ignoring all other caps and adjustments per Ask 1)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. GOVERNING REGULATORY PROVISIONS (12 CFR PART 329)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Definitions (12 CFR § 329.3):
  * Calculation date: Any date on which an FDIC-supervised institution calculates its liquidity coverage ratio under § 329.10.
  * Eligible HQLA: A high-quality liquid asset that meets the operational and eligibility requirements set forth in § 329.22.
  * Fair value: Fair value as determined under GAAP.
- Level 2A Liquid Asset Amount (12 CFR § 329.21(b)(2)):
  "The level 2A liquid asset amount equals 85 percent of the fair value of all level 2A liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA." (Equivalent to a 15% regulatory haircut.)
- Level 2B Liquid Asset Amount (12 CFR § 329.21(b)(3)):
  "The level 2B liquid asset amount equals 50 percent of the fair value of all level 2B liquid assets held by the FDIC-supervised institution as of the calculation date that are eligible HQLA." (Equivalent to a 50% regulatory haircut.)
- Excluded Provisions (per Ask 1 — "Ignoring other caps and adjustments"):
  * Unadjusted excess HQLA amount (40% Level 2 cap under § 329.21(d) and 15% Level 2B cap under § 329.21(e)).
  * Adjusted liquid asset amounts and adjusted excess HQLA amount upon 30-day secured transaction unwinds (§ 329.21(f)-(i)).
  * Operational hedging outflow reductions under § 329.22 (all stated holdings are assumed already confirmed as eligible HQLA per the prompt).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. INPUTS & ASSUMPTIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Input 1 (Prompt): Level 2A eligible HQLA fair value = $80.00 million (USD, GAAP fair value basis, as of the calculation date).
- Input 2 (Prompt): Level 2B eligible HQLA fair value = $30.00 million (USD, GAAP fair value basis, as of the calculation date).
- Working Assumption 1 (Currency): All stated dollar figures ($) are U.S. Dollars (USD).
- Working Assumption 2 (Single-Date Basis): Calculation is performed as of a single calculation date without multi-day averaging.
- Working Assumption 3 (Eligibility): All $80.00 million of Level 2A assets and $30.00 million of Level 2B assets satisfy all § 329.20 asset criteria and § 329.22 operational requirements as stated.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. CALCULATION SCHEDULE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
All figures in USD millions, GAAP fair value input basis, as of the calculation date:

1) Level 2A Liquid Asset Amount (12 CFR § 329.21(b)(2))
   - Fair Value of Eligible Level 2A HQLA (Source: Prompt):          $80.00 million
   - Regulatory Weight (Source: 12 CFR § 329.21(b)(2)):                85% (0.85)
   - Implied Regulatory Haircut:                                       15% ($12.00 million)
   - Arithmetic: $80.00 million * 0.85 = $68.00 million
   - Resulting Level 2A Liquid Asset Amount:                          $68.00 million

2) Level 2B Liquid Asset Amount (12 CFR § 329.21(b)(3))
   - Fair Value of Eligible Level 2B HQLA (Source: Prompt):          $30.00 million
   - Regulatory Weight (Source: 12 CFR § 329.21(b)(3)):                50% (0.50)
   - Implied Regulatory Haircut:                                       50% ($15.00 million)
   - Arithmetic: $30.00 million * 0.50 = $15.00 million
   - Resulting Level 2B Liquid Asset Amount:                          $15.00 million

3) Sum of Level 2A and Level 2B Liquid Asset Amounts (pre-cap, unadjusted)
   - Level 2A Liquid Asset Amount (from Step 1):                      $68.00 million
   - Level 2B Liquid Asset Amount (from Step 2):                      $15.00 million
   - Arithmetic: $68.00 million + $15.00 million = $83.00 million
   - Resulting Sum (Total Level 2 Liquid Asset Amount, pre-cap):      $83.00 million

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. SUMMARY OF RESULTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Level 2A Liquid Asset Amount: $68 million USD ($68,000,000), as of the calculation date, GAAP fair value weighted at 85%.
- Level 2B Liquid Asset Amount: $15 million USD ($15,000,000), as of the calculation date, GAAP fair value weighted at 50%.
- Sum (Level 2A + Level 2B): $83 million USD ($83,000,000), as of the calculation date, ignoring other caps and adjustments.

Control Note for Reviewer: In a full § 329.21 HQLA calculation, total Level 2 assets ($83.00 million) and Level 2B assets ($15.00 million) must subsequently be tested against the Level 1 liquid asset amount (unadjusted and adjusted for 30-day collateralized unwinds) to determine any Level 2 cap excess amount (§ 329.21(d), (h)) and Level 2B cap excess amount (§ 329.21(e), (i)).

findings.question:
1. A covered company subject to the single-counterparty credit limits in 12 CFR Part 252 has $40 billion of tier 1 capital and an $11 billion aggregate net credit exposure to one counterparty. As in force on 2026-11-21, what is its 25% exposure cap in dollars, by how much does the exposure exceed that cap, and is the separate 5% economic-interdependence and control-relationship assessment triggered?
2. The regulatory definition and measurement of tier 1 capital to which the 25% cap applies (determines the cap's dollar amount).
3. The counterparty's status (U.S./non-U.S., affiliate or not), which determines whether the 25% cap and the 5% economic-interdependence threshold apply as assumed.
4. The method by which the $11 billion net exposure was computed, which determines whether it is comparable to the cap.

§ 252.72 Credit exposure limits.




(a) General limit on aggregate net credit exposure.  No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company.





(b) Limit on aggregate net credit exposure of major covered companies to major counterparties.  No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company.

(c) Aggregate net credit exposure  means the sum of all net credit exposures of a covered foreign entity and all of its subsidiaries to a single counterparty as calculated under this subpart.
(d) Bank-eligible investments  means investment securities that a national bank is permitted to purchase, sell, deal in, underwrite, and hold under 12 U.S.C. 24 (Seventh) and 12 CFR part 1.
(e) Capital stock and surplus  means, with respect to a U.S. intermediate holding company, the sum of the following amounts in each case as reported by the U.S. intermediate holding company on the most recent FR Y-9C on a consolidated basis:
(1) The tier 1 capital and tier 2 capital of the U.S. intermediate holding company, as calculated under the capital adequacy guidelines applicable to that U.S. intermediate holding company under subpart O of the Board's Regulation YY (12 CFR part 252, subpart O); and
(2) The excess allowance for loan and lease losses of the U.S. intermediate holding company not included in its tier 2 capital, as calculated under the capital adequacy guidelines applicable to that U.S. intermediate holding company under subpart O of the Board's Regulation YY (12 CFR part 252, subpart O).

As in force on 2026-11-21, what is its 25% exposure cap in dollars, by how much does the exposure exceed that cap, and is the separate 5% economic-interdependence and control-relationship assessment triggered?
2. The regulatory definition and measurement of tier 1 capital to which the 25% cap applies (determines the cap's dollar amount).
3. The counterparty's status (U.S./non-U.S., affiliate or not), which determines whether the 25% cap and the 5% economic-interdependence threshold apply as assumed.
4. The method by which the $11 billion net exposure was computed, which determines whether it is comparable to the cap.
quotes.text: No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company.

quotes.whole:
Subpart Q—Single-Counterparty Credit Limits
Source:
83 FR 38501, Aug. 6, 2018, unless otherwise noted.
§ 252.170 Applicability and general provisions.
(a) In general.
(1) This subpart establishes single counterparty credit limits for a covered foreign entity.
(2) For purposes of this subpart:
(i) Covered foreign entity  means:
(A) A Category II foreign banking organization;
(B) A Category III foreign banking organization;
(C) A foreign banking organization with total consolidated assets that equal or exceed $250 billion;
(D) A Category II U.S. intermediate holding company; and
(E) A Category III U.S. intermediate holding company.
(ii) Major foreign banking organization  means a foreign banking organization that is a covered foreign entity and meets the requirements of § 252.172(c)(3) through (5).
(b) Credit exposure limits.
(1) Section 252.172 establishes credit exposure limits for covered foreign entities and major foreign banking organizations.
(2) A covered foreign entity is required to calculate its aggregate net credit exposure, gross credit exposure, and net credit exposure to a counterparty using the methods in this subpart.

(1) Except as provided in paragraph (a) of this section, no U.S. intermediate holding company that is a covered foreign entity may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the U.S. intermediate holding company.
(2) No foreign banking organization that is a covered foreign entity may permit its combined U.S. operations to have aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the foreign banking organization.

(2) No foreign banking organization that is a covered foreign entity may permit its combined U.S. operations to have aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the foreign banking organization.

quotes.whole: A securities financing transaction must be valued using any of the methods that the covered foreign entity is authorized to use under the Board's Regulation Q (12 CFR part 217, subparts D and E) to value such transactions: (i) (A) As calculated for each transaction, in the case of a securities financing transaction between the covered foreign entity and the counterparty that is not subject to a bilateral netting agreement or does not meet the definition of “repo-style transaction” in § 217.2 of the Board's Regulation Q (12 CFR 217.2); or (B) As calculated for a netting set, in the case of a securities financing transaction between the covered foreign entity and the counterparty that is subject to a bilateral netting agreement with that counterparty and meets the definition of “repo-style transaction” in § 217.2 of the Board's Regulation Q (12 CFR 217.2); (ii) For purposes of paragraph (a)(4)(i) of this section, the covered foreign entity must: (A) Assign a value of zero to any security received from the counterparty that does not meet the definition of “eligible collateral” in § 252.171(l); and (B) Include the value of securities that are eligible collateral received by the covered foreign entity from the counterparty (including any exempt counterparty), calculated in accordance with paragraphs (a)(4)(i) through (iv) of this section, when calculating its gross credit exposure to the issuer of those securities; (iii) Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(4)(i) and (ii) of this section and with respect to each credit transaction, a covered foreign entity's gross credit exposure to a collateral issuer under this paragraph (a)(4) is limited to the covered foreign entity's gross credit exposure to the counterparty on the credit transaction; (iv) In cases where the covered foreign entity receives eligible collateral from a counterparty in addition to the cash or securities received from that counterparty, the counterparty may reduce its gross credit exposure to that counterparty in accordance with § 252.174(b).

verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR PROFESSIONAL REVIEW — This memorandum is prepared for review by a qualified finance, accounting, or regulatory compliance professional. It does not constitute financial, legal, tax, or investment advice.

1. Executive Summary (As in Force on 2026-11-21)
Under 12 CFR Part 252, Subpart H (Single-Counterparty Credit Limits, eCFR text in force on 2026-11-21):
- 25% Exposure Cap (Ask 2): USD 10,000,000,000 (USD 10.0 billion)
- Excess Over 25% Cap (Ask 3): USD 1,000,000,000 (USD 1.0 billion)
- 5% Economic-Interdependence & Control-Relationship Assessment Triggered (Ask 4): Yes (Triggered; aggregate net credit exposure of USD 11,000,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000,000 threshold by USD 9,000,000,000).

2. Inputs, Sources, Basis, Currency, and Period
- Evaluation Date / Regulatory Period: As in force on 2026-11-21 (verified against eCFR 12 CFR Part 252, Subpart H, fetched 2026-11-22).
- Tier 1 Capital: USD 40,000,000,000 (USD 40.0 billion). Source: User request. Currency: USD. Period: As of 2026-11-21 (assumed current regulatory reporting basis). Basis: Assumed to equal regulatory tier 1 capital (Common Equity Tier 1 + Additional Tier 1 capital as defined under 12 CFR Part 252 / Regulation Q, without further adjustment).
- Aggregate Net Credit Exposure to Counterparty: USD 11,000,000,000 (USD 11.0 billion). Source: User request. Currency: USD. Period: As of 2026-11-21. Basis: Assumed to be calculated in accordance with 12 CFR §§ 252.73–252.75 (gross credit exposure reduced by eligible collateral, guarantees, credit derivatives, and netting as permitted under Subpart H).
- General Limit Percentage: 25% (0.25). Source: 12 CFR § 252.72(a).
- Assessment Trigger Percentage: 5% (0.05). Source: 12 CFR § 252.76(a)(1).

3. Calculations and Regulatory Schedule

A. 25% Single-Counterparty Exposure Cap (12 CFR § 252.72(a))
Rule: "No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company."
Arithmetic:
  25% Exposure Cap = 0.25 × USD 40,000,000,000 = USD 10,000,000,000 (USD 10.0 billion)
  Currency: USD | Period: As of 2026-11-21 | Basis: Regulatory limit under 12 CFR § 252.72(a)

B. Exposure Excess Over the 25% Cap
Arithmetic:
  Excess Exposure = Aggregate Net Credit Exposure − 25% Exposure Cap
  Excess Exposure = USD 11,000,000,000 − USD 10,000,000,000 = USD 1,000,000,000 (USD 1.0 billion)
  Exposure as % of Tier 1 Capital = USD 11,000,000,000 / USD 40,000,000,000 = 27.50%
  Excess Percentage Points = 27.50% − 25.00% = 2.50 percentage points (250 bps) over the 25% cap
  Currency: USD | Period: As of 2026-11-21 | Basis: Aggregate net credit exposure vs. 12 CFR § 252.72(a) limit

C. 5% Economic-Interdependence and Control-Relationship Assessment Trigger (12 CFR § 252.76(a)(1))
Rule: "If a covered company has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered company must assess its relationship with the counterparty under paragraph (b)(2) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is economically interdependent with one or more other counterparties of the covered company and under paragraph (c)(1) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is connected by a control relationship with one or more other counterparties."
Arithmetic:
  5% Assessment Threshold = 0.05 × USD 40,000,000,000 = USD 2,000,000,000 (USD 2.0 billion)
  Comparison = USD 11,000,000,000 (Aggregate Net Credit Exposure) > USD 2,000,000,000 (5% Threshold)
  Margin Above 5% Threshold = USD 11,000,000,000 − USD 2,000,000,000 = USD 9,000,000,000 (22.50 percentage points above threshold)
  Verdict: Yes — the separate 5% assessment under 12 CFR § 252.76(a)(1) is triggered.
  Currency: USD | Period: As of 2026-11-21 | Basis: 12 CFR § 252.76(a)(1) trigger test

4. Key Scope Notes and Assumptions for Reviewer Verification
- Entity & Counterparty Classification: Assumed the covered company is a U.S. covered company subject to Subpart H (§ 252.70: G-SIB, Category II BHC, or Category III BHC) and that the 25% general limit (§ 252.72(a)) applies. Note that if the covered company is a major covered company (G-SIB) AND the counterparty is a major counterparty, § 252.72(b) imposes a stricter 15% cap (0.15 × USD 40,000,000,000 = USD 6,000,000,000, resulting in a USD 5,000,000,000 excess). Similarly, if the entity is a U.S. intermediate holding company or foreign banking organization, Subpart Q (§§ 252.170–252.178) imposes analogous 25% general and 5% assessment rules.
- Non-Exempt Counterparty: Assumed the counterparty is not an exempt counterparty under 12 CFR § 252.77 (e.g., U.S. sovereign/agency exposures) and that the USD 11,000,000,000 figure reflects all required Subpart H netting and credit risk mitigation.
- Downstream Compliance Effect: Because the 5% threshold is exceeded, the covered company must perform the § 252.76(b)(2) economic-interdependence and § 252.76(c)(1) control-relationship assessments. If any factor is met, net credit exposures to connected counterparties must be aggregated under § 252.76(a)(2), which could further increase the USD 1,000,000,000 breach. Additionally, the covered company is currently non-compliant with § 252.72(a) by USD 1,000,000,000 and should evaluate cure/reporting obligations under § 252.78.

Question 119.07
Question: Item 402(c)(2)(ix)(A) and Instruction 4 to that item require a company to report as "All Other Compensation" perquisites and personal benefits if the total amount exceeds $10,000, and to identify each such item by type, regardless of the amount. If the $10,000 threshold is otherwise exceeded, must a company list by type those perquisites and personal benefits as to which there was no aggregate incremental cost to the company, or as to which the executive officer fully reimbursed the company for such cost?
Answer: If a perquisite or other personal benefit has no aggregate incremental cost, it must still be separately identified by type. Any item for which an executive officer has actually fully reimbursed the company should not be considered a perquisite or other personal benefit and therefore need not be separately identified by type. In this regard, for example, if a company pays for country club annual dues as well as for meals and incidentals and an executive officer reimburses the cost of meals and incidentals, then the company need not report meals and incidentals as perquisites, although it would continue to report the country club annual dues. If there was no such reimbursement, then the company would need to also report the meals and incidentals as perquisites. [July 3, 2008]

verdict.summary:
MEMORANDUM & COMPLIANCE SCHEDULE: EXECUTIVE PERQUISITE DISCLOSURE UNDER 17 CFR 229.402(c)

NOTICE: This output is a draft prepared for review by a qualified finance, accounting, or legal professional. It is not financial, tax, legal, or investment advice.

1. REGULATORY BASIS, PERIOD, CURRENCY, AND VALUATION BASIS
- Governing Standard: 17 CFR 229.402(c) (Item 402(c) of Regulation S-K), specifically Item 402(c)(2)(ix)(A) and Instruction 4 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix), as verified in the Electronic Code of Federal Regulations (eCFR, fetched 2026-11-22T23:53:07Z) and effective as of 2026-11-21.
- Period: Single covered fiscal year (exact fiscal year-end not specified in request; assumed to be the registrant's most recently completed fiscal year covered by the Summary Compensation Table as of 2026-11-21).
- Currency: United States Dollars (USD).
- Valuation Basis: Aggregate incremental cost to the registrant, per Instruction 4 to Item 402(c)(2)(ix). (Assumed that the $120,000 total, $24,000 item, and $26,000 item represent single, distinct perquisites/personal benefits valued on an aggregate incremental cost basis for a domestic registrant subject to Item 402(c) rather than an alternative regime.)

2. SUMMARY OF CONCLUSIONS
- Ask 2 (May the registrant exclude perquisites altogether?): No. Total perquisites of $120,000 USD are not less than the $10,000 USD exclusion threshold.
- Ask 3 (Footnote quantification threshold): $25,000 USD (computed as the greater of $25,000 USD or 10% of $120,000 USD = $12,000 USD).
- Ask 4 (Which of the two items—$24,000 or $26,000—must be quantified?): The $26,000 item only ($26,000 USD > $25,000 USD threshold). Both items (and all other perquisites regardless of amount) must still be identified by type.

3. STEP-BY-STEP THRESHOLD ARITHMETIC & REGULATORY APPLICATION

Step A: Exclusion Test (Item 402(c)(2)(ix)(A) & Instruction 4)
- Rule: "Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type."
- Source Figure: Total NEO perquisites and personal benefits = $120,000 USD (per request facts).
- Threshold Figure: $10,000 USD (per Instruction 4 to 17 CFR 229.402(c)(2)(ix)).
- Comparison: $120,000 USD >= $10,000 USD (exceeds threshold by $120,000 - $10,000 = $110,000 USD).
- Result: Exclusion is NOT permitted. The full $120,000 USD must be included in Column (i) (All Other Compensation) of the Summary Compensation Table, and every perquisite/personal benefit (regardless of dollar amount) must be identified by type.

Step B: Footnote Quantification Threshold Calculation (Instruction 4)
- Rule: "If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote."
- Fixed Floor: $25,000 USD (per Instruction 4 to 17 CFR 229.402(c)(2)(ix)).
- 10% Percentage Test: 10% x $120,000 USD (source: total NEO perquisites from request) = 0.10 x $120,000 = $12,000 USD.
- Applicable Threshold: max($25,000 USD, $12,000 USD) = $25,000 USD.

Step C: Item-by-Item Quantification Test & Reconciliation Schedule
All figures in USD for the single covered fiscal year, aggregate incremental cost basis:

1. Perquisite Item A (Specified in request)
   - Source: Request facts
   - Amount: $24,000 USD
   - Share of Total: $24,000 / $120,000 = 20.00%
   - Test vs. Threshold ($25,000 USD): $24,000 USD <= $25,000 USD (short of threshold by $25,000 - $24,000 = $1,000 USD)
   - Required Treatment: Include in Column (i) total; identify by type in footnote; footnote dollar quantification NOT required.

2. Perquisite Item B (Specified in request)
   - Source: Request facts
   - Amount: $26,000 USD
   - Share of Total: $26,000 / $120,000 = 21.67%
   - Test vs. Threshold ($25,000 USD): $26,000 USD > $25,000 USD (exceeds threshold by $26,000 - $25,000 = $1,000 USD)
   - Required Treatment: Include in Column (i) total; identify by type in footnote; MUST quantify dollar amount ($26,000 USD) in footnote AND describe methodology for computing aggregate incremental cost.

3. Remaining Other Perquisites (Reconciling Balance)

verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE OR ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL (NOT FINANCIAL, TAX, OR INVESTMENT ADVICE)

Regulatory Capital Minimums Memorandum — Calendar Year 2014 (OCC 12 CFR Part 3)
Entity Scope: Advanced approaches national bank that is not a savings and loan holding company (SLHC)
Effective Period: January 1, 2014 through December 31, 2014 (Calendar Year 2014)
Basis & Units: Regulatory capital ratios expressed as percentages of risk-weighted assets (dimensionless percentage ratios; no currency unit applies), calculated on a transitional basis under 12 CFR Part 3, excluding capital conservation buffers, countercyclical capital buffers, and any other add-ons.

1. Ask 1 — Applicable Minimum CET1 and Tier 1 Capital Ratios (Jan 1 – Dec 31, 2014)
Per 12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) (verified across the 2024 CFR edition, 2026 CFR edition, current eCFR, and partially excerpted in the 2014 CFR edition PDF for § 3.1):
- Quoted rule text: "From January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2014, maintain a minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4 percent, a minimum tier 1 capital ratio of 5.5 percent, a minimum total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a minimum leverage ratio of 4 percent;"
- Minimum Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Capital Ratio: 4% (4.0%)
  - Source: 12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)
  - Basis: Regulatory transition minimum for CY 2014, excluding buffers/add-ons; numerator = CET1 capital (12 CFR Part 3, Subpart C, subject to Subpart G transition adjustments), denominator = advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets (12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(i), Subpart E and Subpart F if applicable, as standardized RWA under Subpart D began January 1, 2015).
- Minimum Tier 1 Capital Ratio: 5.5%
  - Source: 12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A)
  - Basis: Regulatory transition minimum for CY 2014, excluding buffers/add-ons; numerator = Tier 1 capital (CET1 capital + Additional Tier 1 capital), denominator = advanced approaches total risk-weighted assets.
- Arithmetic Check (Capital Stack Composition): Tier 1 minimum (5.5%) - CET1 minimum (4.0%) = 1.5 percentage points maximum Tier 1 minimum requirement satisfiable by Additional Tier 1 capital when CET1 is at the 4.0% floor.

2. Ask 2 — Corresponding Minimum Ratios in the Text of 12 CFR Part 3 Reproduced on 'the Cited Page' [BLOCKED]
- Status: Cannot be answered with available grounding.
- Reason: The request refers to "the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page," but neither the request nor the project documentation identifies or provides that page (missing URL, CFR edition/page number, Federal Register citation, or excerpt).
- Reference Comparison for Reviewer (once the cited page is supplied):
  1) If the cited page reproduces 12 CFR § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) (Timing — 2014 transition period): CET1 minimum = 4% (4.0%); Tier 1 minimum = 5.5% (matches Ask 1; difference = 0.0 percentage points).
  2) If the cited page reproduces 12 CFR § 3.10(a)(1) (General / steady-state minimum capital requirements, present in 2024 CFR, 2026 CFR, and current eCFR): CET1 minimum = 4.5%; Tier 1 minimum = 6% (6.0%) (variance vs. 2014 transition minimums: 4.5% - 4.0% = +0.5 percentage points CET1; 6.0% - 5.5% = +0.5 percentage points Tier 1).

3. Constraint Verification (Ask 3 — Ignore Buffers and Other Add-Ons)
All figures above exclude the capital conservation buffer, countercyclical capital buffer, global systemically important bank (G-SIB) surcharge, and any individual minimum capital ratios under Subpart H (12 CFR § 3.403).

blocked_on.why: Ask 2 ('what are the corresponding minimum ratios in the text of 12 CFR Part 3 reproduced on the cited page?'): Neither the request nor the project documentation identifies or supplies 'the cited page' (no URL, CFR edition/page citation, Federal Register page, or reproduced excerpt is provided). Because 12 CFR Part 3 states 4% CET1 / 5.5% Tier 1 in § 3.1(f)(1)(iii)(A) for calendar year 2014 and 4.5% CET1 / 6% Tier 1 in § 3.10(a)(1) as general minimums, identifying which page/section is cited is required to answer Ask 2 without guessing.

From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits.
At the Spring Budget 2021, the Corporation Tax main rate for non-ring fence profits was increased to 25% for profits above £250,000.
A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less.
Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. This provides a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate.

What Marginal Relief is
From 1 April 2023 the Corporation Tax rate changes to:
19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate)
25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)
Marginal Relief provides a gradual increase in Corporation Tax rate between the small profits rate and the main rate — this allows you to reduce your rate from the 25% main rate.
Who can claim Marginal Relief
Your company or organisation may be able to claim Marginal Relief if its taxable profits from 1 April 2023 are between:
£50,000 (the lower limit)
£250,000 (the upper limit)

quotes.whole:
Tax rates
From 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023, there was a unified rate of CT. On 1 April 2015 the rate was set at 20% and this reduced to 19% on 1 April 2017. This 19% rate was in place for the financial years covered by the time series included in this publication.
From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits. At the Spring Budget 2021, the government announced that the Corporation Tax main rate for non-ring fence profits would increase to 25% for profits above £250,000. A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less.
Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. Further information on Corporation Tax rates can be found on GOV.UK
Different tax rates apply to companies with income and gains from oil and gas and gas extraction or oil rights, known as ‘ring-fence’ companies. These companies are also subject to a Supplementary tax charge on their ring-fenced profits. More information about ring-fence companies and CT statistics can be found on GOV.UK.
Payment and assessment arrangements

quotes.whole:
CTA10/PART 3A
With effect from 1 April 2023, the standard small profits rate of Corporation Tax for non-ring fence profits has been reintroduced at CTA10/PART3A by FA2021/S6 and SCH1 ensuring that companies with smaller profits pay CT a lower rate when the main rate is increased from the same date.
The small profits rate previously applied for financial years up to and including 2014.  For further details, see CTM03500 onwards.
The rules that apply to the standard small profits rate largely replicate the earlier scheme and distinguish between:
total taxable profits, and
augmented profits - defined at CTA10/S18L as the total taxable profits plus exempt distributions of a qualifying kind received by the company that are not excluded.
Further details of what is meant by profits in this context are at CTM03915.
Where the profits do not exceed a set lower limit, the total taxable profits are charged at a lower rate of CT, known as the standard small profits rate.  This is distinguished from the small ring fence profits rate, CTA10/S279A.
Where the profits exceed a set upper limit, the total taxable profits are charged at the CT main rate.
Marginal Relief

Skip contents
Contents

Rates
The Corporation Tax rate for company profits is 25%
You pay Corporation Tax at the rates that applied in your company’s accounting period for Corporation Tax.
If your company made more than £250,000 profit, you’ll pay the main rate of Corporation Tax.
If your company made a profit of £50,000 or less, you’ll pay the ‘small profits rate’, which is 19%.
You may be entitled to ‘Marginal Relief’ if your profits were between £50,000 and £250,000.
The £50,000 and £250,000 profit thresholds are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and by the total number of ‘associated companies’ your company has.
There are different rates for ‘ring fence’ profits of companies involved in oil rights or extraction in the UK or UK continental shelf.
You may be able to get deductions or claim tax credits on your Corporation Tax. These are known as allowances and reliefs.
Previous rates
From 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023, a single rate of Corporation Tax applied to all companies.
The rate you pay on profits from before 1 April 2015 depends on the size of your profits.

verdict.summary:
DRAFT FOR QUALIFIED FINANCE OR ACCOUNTING PROFESSIONAL REVIEW. THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT FINANCIAL, TAX OR INVESTMENT ADVICE.

================================================================================
TAX TECHNICAL MEMO: UK CORPORATION TAX RATES (NON-RING FENCE PROFITS)
Rules Applying From 1 April 2023
================================================================================

1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & DIRECT ANSWERS

Based on HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) published guidance, *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026) and supporting HMRC guidance on Marginal Relief:

- Is there still a single Corporation Tax rate (non-ring fence profits, from 1 April 2023)?
  No. From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits. (For context, a single unified rate of 19% applied from 1 April 2017 to 31 March 2023, following a 20% unified rate from 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2017.)

- Rate for profits of £50,000 or less:
  19% (the small profits rate).
  - Period: Financial Years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 (1 April 2023 onwards).
  - Currency & Basis: GBP (£); non-ring fence profits for a standalone company with a 12-month accounting period.
  - Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax) and *Corporation Tax rates, expenses and reliefs* (https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates/rates).

- Main rate for profits above £250,000:
  25% (the main rate).
  - Period: Financial Years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 (1 April 2023 onwards).
  - Currency & Basis: GBP (£); non-ring fence profits for a standalone company with a 12-month accounting period.
  - Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026).

- Treatment of profits between £50,000 and £250,000:
  Companies with profits between £50,000 (the Marginal Relief lower limit) and £250,000 (the Marginal Relief upper limit) are charged Corporation Tax at the 25% main rate, reduced by Marginal Relief using HMRC's standard fraction of 3/200 (0.015 or 1.5%). This produces a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate from 19% at £50,000 to 25% at £250,000.
  - Period: Financial Years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026.
  - Currency & Basis: GBP (£); non-ring fence profits for a standalone company with a 12-month accounting period.
  - Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026) and *Marginal Relief for Corporation Tax* (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/corporation-tax-marginal-relief).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. SCHEDULE OF RATES, LIMITS AND FRACTIONS (NON-RING FENCE PROFITS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Source: HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* (updated 1 April 2026).
Scope: Non-ring fence profits (excluding ring fence oil extraction/rights profits and excluding the 20% special rate for unit trusts and open-ended investment companies).
Period: Corporation Tax financial years starting 1 April 2023, 2024, 2025, and 2026 (each financial year runs 1 April to 31 March).
Currency: GBP (£).

  Band / Parameter                           Rate / Value     Basis
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Small profits rate (<= £50,000)            19%              Total taxable profits
  Main rate (> £250,000)                     25%              Total taxable profits
  Marginal Relief lower limit                £50,000          Augmented profits*
  Marginal Relief upper limit                £250,000         Augmented profits*
  Standard fraction                          3/200 (1.5%)     Statutory fraction
  Prior single rate (FY 2022: 1 Apr 2022     19%              All non-ring fence
    to 31 Mar 2023)                                           profits
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * Note on wording and profit basis: While the summary table in HMRC's
    *Corporation Tax rates and allowances* labels the small profits rate as
    '(companies with profits under £50,000)', the body text of the same page,
    *Corporation Tax rates, expenses and reliefs*, and HMRC's Company Taxation
    Manual (CTM03905) confirm the threshold is profits of £50,000 or less
    ('do not exceed a set lower limit'). CTM03905 notes that the regime
    distinguishes between 'total taxable profits' (on which tax is charged) and
    'augmented profits' (CTA10/S18L: total taxable profits plus non-excluded
    exempt qualifying distributions) for determining which threshold applies.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. ARITHMETIC VERIFICATION OF MARGINAL RELIEF BOUNDARIES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Assumed Basis for Illustration: Standalone company (0 associated companies), 12-month accounting period wholly within FY 2023 to FY 2026, non-ring fence profits, GBP (£), with augmented profits equal to total taxable profits (i.e. no exempt qualifying distributions).

Sources of inputs:
- Main rate = 25% (HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances*)
- Small profits rate = 19% (HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances*)
- Lower limit = £50,000; Upper limit = £250,000 (HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances*)
- Standard fraction = 3/200 = 0.015 (HMRC *Corporation Tax rates and allowances*)

Boundary Check 1 — At the Lower Limit (£50,000):
- Tax at main rate: £50,000 x 25% = £12,500
- Marginal Relief: (£250,000 - £50,000) x (3 / 200) = £200,000 x 0.015 = £3,000
- Net Corporation Tax: £12,500 - £3,000 = £9,500
- Effective CT rate: £9,500 / £50,000 = 19.00% (matches the 19% small profits rate)

Boundary Check 2 — At the Upper Limit (£250,000):
- Tax at main rate: £250,000 x 25% = £62,500
- Marginal Relief: (£250,000 - £250,000) x (3 / 200) = £0 x 0.015 = £0
- Net Corporation Tax: £62,500 - £0 = £62,500
- Effective CT rate: £62,500 / £250,000 = 25.00% (matches the 25% main rate)

Effective Marginal Tax Rate Across the £50,000 to £250,000 Band:
- Incremental profit across band: £250,000 - £50,000 = £200,000
- Incremental tax across band: £62,500 - £9,500 = £53,000
- Effective marginal rate on profits within the band: £53,000 / £200,000 = 26.50%
  (Arithmetic check: 25.00% main rate + 1.50% withdrawal of relief via 3/200 fraction = 26.50%)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. KEY STATUTORY & COMPLIANCE ADJUSTMENTS TO CHECK ON APPLICATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Before applying the £50,000 and £250,000 thresholds to an actual company return, the reviewing professional should verify the following HMRC rules noted in the guidance:

1. Associated Companies (https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates/rates):
   The £50,000 and £250,000 thresholds are proportionately reduced by the total number of associated companies (dividing each limit by 1 plus the number of associated companies).

2. Short Accounting Periods (https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates/rates):
   For accounting periods shorter than 12 months, the £50,000 and £250,000 thresholds are proportionately reduced according to the length of the accounting period.

3. Augmented Profits & Exempt Distributions (CTM03905 / *Marginal Relief for Corporation Tax*):
   The thresholds are tested against augmented profits (total taxable profits plus qualifying exempt distributions received from unrelated/unassociated companies, per CTA10/S18L), not solely total taxable profits. Where augmented profits differ from total taxable profits, Marginal Relief is scaled by (total taxable profits / augmented profits).

4. Accounting Periods Straddling 31 March 2023 (https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates/rates):
   Where an accounting period straddles 31 March 2023 (for example, 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023), profits are time-apportioned by days between the financial year starting 1 April 2022 (90 days at the 19% single rate) and the financial year starting 1 April 2023 (275 days under the post-1 April 2023 rules, with thresholds scaled for the 275-day part).

5. Out-of-Scope Entities / Profits:
   - Ring fence companies (UK/UKCS oil extraction or oil rights) remain subject to separate ring fence rates (19% small ring fence rate, 30% main ring fence rate, 11/400 fraction, plus Supplementary Charge).
   - Unit trusts and open-ended investment companies remain subject to a special rate of 20%.

results.value: Taxed at the 25% main rate, reduced by Marginal Relief (standard fraction 3/200)

§§ 3.4-3.9 [Reserved]
Subpart B—Capital Ratio Requirements and Buffers
Source:
78 FR 62157, 62273, Oct. 11, 2013, unless otherwise noted.
§ 3.10 Minimum capital requirements.
(a) Minimum capital requirements.
(1) A national bank or Federal savings association must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:
(i) A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent.
(ii) A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent.
(iii) A total capital ratio of 8 percent.
(iv) A leverage ratio of 4 percent.
(v) For advanced approaches national banks or Federal savings associations or, for Category III OCC-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent.
(vi) For Federal savings associations, a tangible capital ratio of 1.5 percent.
(2) A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in § 3.12), that is subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework (as defined in § 3.12), is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in this paragraph (a).
(b) Standardized capital ratio calculations.  Other than as provided in paragraph (c) of this section:
